questions.question: What occurs at the quantum level when a sample containing ¹H nuclei (spin I = 1/2) is placed in a strong external magnetic field (B₀)?

options.label: A
options.text: The nuclear magnetic moments quantize into two discrete energy states: low-energy α-spin (aligned with B₀) and high-energy β-spin (opposed to B₀).

options.label: B
options.text: All protons immediately emit electrons.

options.label: C
options.text: The protons merge into a single nuclear dication.

options.label: D
options.text: The protons stop rotating completely.

questions.correct_answer: The nuclear magnetic moments quantize into two discrete energy states: low-energy α-spin (aligned with B₀) and high-energy β-spin (opposed to B₀).
questions.explanation: Spin-1/2 nuclei align either parallel (α, low energy) or antiparallel (β, high energy) to the external magnetic field B₀.

questions.question: Why do protons attached to electron-dense sp³ carbons resonate upfield (lower δ, closer to TMS) than protons attached to electronegative atoms?

options.label: A
options.text: Protons with high electron density absorb radiofrequency faster.

options.label: B
options.text: Surrounding valence electrons circulate in response to B₀, generating an induced local magnetic field that opposes B₀ and shields the nucleus (B_effective = B₀ - B_local).

options.label: C
options.text: Electronegative atoms add neutrons to the proton nucleus.

options.label: D
options.text: Electron-rich protons have smaller nuclear masses.

questions.correct_answer: Surrounding valence electrons circulate in response to B₀, generating an induced local magnetic field that opposes B₀ and shields the nucleus (B_effective = B₀ - B_local).
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic electron circulation shields the nucleus from the external field, requiring higher applied field / lower δ to achieve resonance.

questions.question: What physical phenomenon causes aromatic protons on benzene to resonate significantly downfield at δ 7.27 ppm?

options.label: A
options.text: The applied field induces a diamagnetic circulation of 6π electrons (ring current), which creates an induced magnetic field that reinforces B₀ outside the ring perimeter.

options.label: B
options.text: Benzene protons are attached to sp³ carbons.

options.label: C
options.text: Aromatic protons form hydrogen bonds with CDCl₃.

options.label: D
options.text: Benzene has no valence electrons to shield the protons.

questions.correct_answer: The applied field induces a diamagnetic circulation of 6π electrons (ring current), which creates an induced magnetic field that reinforces B₀ outside the ring perimeter.
questions.explanation: The induced magnetic field from the circulating π electrons adds to the external field outside the ring perimeter (deshielding cone).

questions.question: Why does the aldehyde proton (-CHO) appear uniquely far downfield at δ 9–10 ppm in ¹H NMR?

options.label: A
options.text: Aldehyde protons are fully ionized in solution.

options.label: B
options.text: A combination of powerful inductive electron withdrawal by the carbonyl oxygen and magnetic anisotropy from the C=O π electron circulation deshields the proton.

options.label: C
options.text: The aldehyde proton is shielded by nitrogen lone pairs.

options.label: D
options.text: The aldehyde proton undergoes rapid radical exchange.

questions.correct_answer: A combination of powerful inductive electron withdrawal by the carbonyl oxygen and magnetic anisotropy from the C=O π electron circulation deshields the proton.
questions.explanation: The polarized C=O bond pulls electron density away, while magnetic anisotropy reinforces the external magnetic field at the proton position.

questions.question: How is spin information transmitted between neighboring protons to produce multiplets (n+1 rule)?

options.label: A
options.text: Through magnetic radiation emitted through empty space.

options.label: B
options.text: Through physical collision of the two proton nuclei.

options.label: C
options.text: Through the polarization of intervening bonding electrons: the spin orientation of proton A slightly polarizes the C-H and C-C σ electrons that contact proton B.

options.label: D
options.text: Through rapid chemical exchange of hydrogen atoms.

questions.correct_answer: Through the polarization of intervening bonding electrons: the spin orientation of proton A slightly polarizes the C-H and C-C σ electrons that contact proton B.
questions.explanation: Scalar J-coupling is mediated through bonding electrons via the Fermi contact interaction across 2 or 3 σ bonds.

questions.topic: Hydroxyl Proton Chemical Exchange in D₂O
questions.question: Why does adding a drop of D₂O to an NMR sample of an alcohol cause the O-H peak to vanish?

options.label: A
options.text: D₂O destroys the magnetic field of the spectrometer.

options.label: B
options.text: D₂O precipitates the alcohol from solution.

options.label: C
options.text: Rapid, uncatalogued chemical exchange replaces the hydroxyl proton with deuterium (R-OH + D₂O ⇌ R-OD + HOD); deuterium resonates at a completely different frequency.

options.label: D
options.text: D₂O oxidizes the alcohol to a ketone.

questions.correct_answer: Rapid, uncatalogued chemical exchange replaces the hydroxyl proton with deuterium (R-OH + D₂O ⇌ R-OD + HOD); deuterium resonates at a completely different frequency.
questions.explanation: Deuterium exchange replaces ¹H with ²H, eliminating the ¹H NMR resonance signal for the exchangeable hydroxyl proton.

questions.question: Why do the two methylene protons of (S)-1,2-dichloropropane appear as two distinct multiplets with different chemical shifts?

options.label: A
options.text: Because the molecule is a racemic mixture.

options.label: B
options.text: Because the carbon-carbon bond cannot rotate.

options.label: C
options.text: Because replacement of each proton individually generates a pair of diastereomers, proving that the two protons experience non-superimposable, diastereomeric spatial environments.

options.label: D
options.text: Because one proton is bonded to chlorine.

questions.correct_answer: Because replacement of each proton individually generates a pair of diastereomers, proving that the two protons experience non-superimposable, diastereomeric spatial environments.
questions.explanation: Diastereotopic protons reside in stereochemically distinct environments relative to adjacent chiral centers, making them magnetically non-equivalent.

questions.question: How does the DEPT-135 NMR pulse sequence differentiate between CH₃, CH₂, and CH carbon atoms?

options.label: A
options.text: It detects carbon-carbon double bonds exclusively.

options.label: B
options.text: It utilizes variable-angle polarization transfer from coupled protons: CH₃ and CH carbons appear as positive peaks, CH₂ carbons appear inverted (negative), and quaternary carbons vanish.

options.label: C
options.text: It measures the radioactive decay rate of ¹³C.

options.label: D
options.text: It heats the sample to evaporate primary carbons.

questions.correct_answer: It utilizes variable-angle polarization transfer from coupled protons: CH₃ and CH carbons appear as positive peaks, CH₂ carbons appear inverted (negative), and quaternary carbons vanish.
questions.explanation: DEPT-135 uses a 135° proton pulse to invert the phase of CH₂ signals while keeping CH and CH₃ positive and eliminating non-protonated carbons.

questions.question: What is the purpose of applying continuous broadband radiofrequency radiation at proton frequencies during ¹³C NMR acquisition?

options.label: A
options.text: To prevent the sample from catching fire.

options.label: B
options.text: To measure the molecular weight of the solvent.

options.label: C
options.text: To split carbon peaks into triplets.

options.label: D
options.text: To rapidly saturate and average all ¹H spin states to zero, collapsing all ¹³C-¹H multiplets into sharp singlets and enhancing sensitivity via the Nuclear Overhauser Effect (NOE).

questions.correct_answer: To rapidly saturate and average all ¹H spin states to zero, collapsing all ¹³C-¹H multiplets into sharp singlets and enhancing sensitivity via the Nuclear Overhauser Effect (NOE).
questions.explanation: Broadband decoupling simplifies the spectrum to single lines per distinct carbon while NOE increases carbon signal intensity up to 200%.

questions.question: What physical property does the vertical step height of an NMR integration curve represent?

options.label: A
options.text: The molecular weight of the compound.

options.label: B
options.text: The boiling point of the functional group.

options.label: C
options.text: The area under the resonance peak, which is strictly directly proportional to the relative number of hydrogen nuclei giving rise to that signal.

options.label: D
options.text: The rate of chemical reaction.

questions.correct_answer: The area under the resonance peak, which is strictly directly proportional to the relative number of hydrogen nuclei giving rise to that signal.
questions.explanation: NMR peak area is directly proportional to the number of resonant protons, allowing precise determination of hydrogen ratios in the molecule.
